author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix:
A rumored leak of new changes coming to Xbox Game Pass has the internet speculating on the future of the service. The biggest change reportedly coming is the loss of Day One games on the service, across all tiers. There will also be the introduction of a cheaper ad-supported tier, but online play, cloud streaming, and family accounts will all be extra add-ons. In other news, the CEO of Bulkhead, the developers of Wardogs, has defended development crunch by saying it's more of a 'balancing act,' by giving developers room to step back when things get too intense. The issue of crunch has plagued game development for decades as games, especially multi-million-dollar AAA games fall behind in development. And finally, Resident Evil direct Zach Cregger has just the actress in mind if he ever needs to cast for RE Village's Lady Dimitrescu.
title: Microsoft Rumored to Be Killing Day One Games on Xbox Game Pass - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
When Xbox snatched Hideo Kojima’s PHYSINT out from under Sony’s nose, it felt less like a standard corporate pivot and more like WCW poaching Hulk Hogan at the onset of the Monday Night Wars. Snagging the auteur behind Metal Gear Solid, the very franchise that established PlayStation's reputation for prestige storytellingm, is a massive PR flex loaded with symbolism, proving Microsoft is eager to play the aggressive underdog. But as wrestling history proves, signing the biggest icon in the business doesn't guarantee a long-term win if internal hubris and ballooning budgets take over the show.

This video breaks down the full story behind Hideo Kojima's PHYSINT moving to Xbox, Sony's surprising cancellation of Metal Gear Solid's spiritual successor, and what it means for the future of PlayStation and Xbox. With new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma securing Kojima Productions’ upcoming action-espionage game alongside OD, Microsoft is attempting a massive reset of its exclusive lineup. With Xbox loo
title: This PHYSINT What People Want, Sony

Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave reviewed by Brendan Graeber on Nintendo Switch 2.

"Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave builds upon its strategic arts in ways I couldn’t have anticipated. It’s never satisfied to make me grow only as a battlefield tactician, or only in my ability to manage my time between skirmishes wisely, but both in perfect harmony. Every time I turned around, I was being given more challenges to face and more tools to master in order to overcome them. The many unique twists of each hero’s story path had me eager to see all the ways those journeys differed from each other, making the grand culmination in the final act hit so damn well. Planning out my expeditions across an imposing map became an unexpected highlight that not only hooked me, but rewarded my persistence by continuing to expand all the ways I could direct my armies as I tried to stay on top of newly emerging threats. The scope of both its formidably challenging battles and intricate management systems would be w
title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Review

author: IGN
description:
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter reviewed by George Yang on PlayStation 5, also on PC, Nintendo Switch, and Switch 2.

"There’s never been a better time to get into the Trails series than now. Following the outstanding Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter remake, the Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter remake is just as fantastic. It captures everything that made the original so endearing, and it’s not just a fresh coat of paint. It’s a complete makeover with a polished art style and stellar voice direction that enhance its elegant storytelling and charismatic cast. It also capitalizes on over two decades worth of gameplay iterations and puts them into one action-packed yet emotional adventure. Despite a temporary lull in its penultimate act, that doesn’t stop 2nd Chapter from being a quintessential Trails game and RPG in its own right."

#IGN #Gaming
title: Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter Review
